questions.answer: Reasonably, yes, though it depends on the situation. I'm quite patient with people, but I can get [[restless]] when I'm stuck waiting, in traffic for instance. It's something I'm consciously working on.

questions.q: Is patience important in your job?
questions.answer: Hugely important. Visa and admission processes can take months, and students naturally get anxious. Part of my role is reassuring them and staying calm and [[composed]], even when they call me for the tenth time about the same thing.

questions.q: Were you patient as a child?
questions.answer: Not in the slightest. I wanted everything immediately, whether it was my food, a new toy or my turn at batting. My parents constantly told me to wait, which I found completely [[infuriating]] at the time.

questions.q: Who is the most patient person you know?
questions.answer: My mother, without question. She looks after our home, helps care for my grandparents and still finds time for everyone. I've never seen her lose her temper, which is honestly [[admirable]] given how much she juggles.

questions.q: Do you think people are less patient nowadays than in the past?
questions.answer: I'd say so. We're used to [[instant gratification]] now, with fast internet, quick deliveries and endless entertainment on our phones. As a result, waiting even a few minutes can feel unbearable to many people.
